title: Energy, Work and Power Module 1 Lesson 1: Work Done by Force at Angle custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: A crate is pulled across a smooth horizontal floor by a horizontal cable with a constant tension of $85\text{ N}$. The crate moves a distance of $16\text{ m}$. Calculate the work done by the tension in the cable.

A sledge is pulled along a flat horizontal snowy track by a rope inclined at $35^\circ$ above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is $60\text{ N}$. The sledge moves a distance of $25\text{ m}$. Calculate the work done by the tension in the rope.

A gardener pushes a lawn roller across horizontal ground by applying a constant force of $120\text{ N}$ along the handle, which is inclined at $40^\circ$ below the horizontal. The roller moves forward through a distance of $18\text{ m}$. Calculate the work done by the pushing force.

A box is pulled along a horizontal floor for a distance of $14\text{ m}$ by a constant tension of $45\text{ N}$ inclined at an angle of $\theta^\circ$ above the horizontal. The work done by the tension is $420\text{ J}$. Find the value of $\theta$.

A cart is pulled a distance of $12\text{ m}$ up a smooth slope inclined at $25^\circ$ to the horizontal by a rope acting parallel to the line of greatest slope. The tension in the rope is $50\text{ N}$. Calculate the work done by the tension, and state the work done by the normal contact force on the cart.

A trolley moves in a straight line along a horizontal track at a constant speed of $2.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $16\text{ s}$. It is pulled by a cable with a constant tension of $70\text{ N}$ inclined at $28^\circ$ above the horizontal. Calculate the work done by the tension in the cable during this $16\text{ s}$ period.

questions.prompt: A crate of mass $30\text{ kg}$ is pulled along a straight horizontal floor by a rope inclined at $25^\circ$ above the horizontal. The tension in the rope is $80\text{ N}$. The crate moves at a constant speed of $1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for a duration of $10\text{ s}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the distance travelled by the crate and calculate the work done by the tension in the rope.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the crate moves at constant speed, state the magnitude of the constant resisting force opposing motion, and find the work done against this resistance.

questions.prompt: A block of mass $20\text{ kg}$ rests on a rough horizontal surface where the coefficient of friction is $\mu = 0.25$. A pulling force of magnitude $P = 70\text{ N}$ acts on the block at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. The block is dragged a distance of $8\text{ m}$ along the surface. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the normal contact force exerted by the surface on the block, and show that the frictional force acting on the block has magnitude $41.25\text{ N}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the pulling force $P$, and the work done against friction over the $8\text{ m}$ displacement.

questions.prompt: A package of mass $12\text{ kg}$ is pulled up a rough plane inclined at $15^\circ$ to the horizontal. The pulling force has magnitude $95\text{ N}$ and acts at an angle of $20^\circ$ above the line of greatest slope of the plane. The package moves a distance of $6\text{ m}$ up the slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the $95\text{ N}$ pulling force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done against gravity as the package moves $6\text{ m}$ up the slope, and determine the vertical height gained.

questions.prompt: A worker moves a heavy toolbox of mass $40\text{ kg}$ across a rough horizontal concrete floor by applying a constant force of magnitude $150\text{ N}$ inclined at $22^\circ$ below the horizontal. The toolbox is moved through a distance of $12\text{ m}$. The coefficient of friction between the toolbox and the concrete floor is $\mu = 0.28$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the normal contact force exerted by the floor on the toolbox, and find the work done against friction during the $12\text{ m}$ movement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done by the $150\text{ N}$ pushing force, and determine whether the work done by the pushing force exceeds the work done against friction.

questions.prompt: A sledge of mass $25\text{ kg}$ is pulled up a smooth slope inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}$. The pulling force $F = 200\text{ N}$ acts horizontally. The sledge moves a distance of $10\text{ m}$ up the slope. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the angle between the horizontal force and the direction of motion along the slope, and calculate the work done by the $200\text{ N}$ force.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the work done against gravity as the sledge ascends the $10\text{ m}$, and find the net work done on the sledge.

questions.prompt: A container of mass $50\text{ kg}$ is pulled in a straight line along a horizontal dockside at a constant speed of $2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $15\text{ s}$. The pulling force has magnitude $T\text{ N}$ and is inclined at an angle $\theta$ above the horizontal. The total work done by the pulling force over the $15\text{ s}$ interval is $2400\text{ J}$. The dockside surface is rough with coefficient of friction $\mu = 0.2$. Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the distance travelled by the container, and express $T\cos\theta$ in terms of the work done, finding its exact numerical value.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the condition that the container moves at constant speed, formulate an equation involving $T\sin\theta$, and hence determine the value of $\theta$ in degrees and the magnitude of $T$.

questions.prompt:
A sledge of mass $18\text{ kg}$ is pulled up a rough inclined plane of length $20\text{ m}$ inclined at $14^\circ$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the sledge and the inclined plane is $\mu = 0.15$. The motion occurs in two successive stages:
- In Stage 1, the sledge is pulled from the bottom of the incline through the first $12\text{ m}$ by a rope parallel to the line of greatest slope with a constant tension of $T_1 = 110\text{ N}$.
- In Stage 2, the rope is adjusted so that it pulls at an angle of $25^\circ$ above the incline with a constant tension of $T_2 = 130\text{ N}$ for the remaining $8\text{ m}$ to the top of the incline.
Take $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For Stage 1, calculate the work done by the tension $T_1$, the normal contact force $R_1$, and the work done against friction over the $12\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For Stage 2, calculate the normal contact force $R_2$, the work done by the tension $T_2$, and the work done against friction over the $8\text{ m}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the total work done by the tension forces across the entire $20\text{ m}$ journey, and the total work done against gravity.
